items.name: C#
items.description: Object-oriented, statically typed programming language developed by Microsoft for the .NET platform, used to build web, desktop, mobile, and game applications.

items.name: COBOL
items.description: Older procedural programming language designed for business and administrative data processing, still widely used in legacy mainframe systems in banking and government.

items.name: Dart
items.description: Object-oriented programming language developed by Google, primarily used with the Flutter framework to build cross-platform mobile, web, and desktop applications.

items.name: Go
items.description: Statically typed, compiled programming language created at Google, valued for its simplicity and built-in support for concurrency; commonly used for backend services and infrastructure tooling.

items.name: Groovy
items.description: Dynamic programming language that runs on the Java Virtual Machine and interoperates closely with Java, often used for scripting, testing, and build automation such as Gradle.

items.name: Java
items.description: Object-oriented, platform-independent programming language widely used for enterprise systems, Android app development, and large-scale backend services.

items.name: Kotlin
items.description: Statically typed programming language that runs on the JVM and interoperates with Java, officially supported by Google as a primary language for Android development.

items.name: Lua
items.description: Lightweight, embeddable scripting language commonly used to add configurable logic and extensibility to applications and video games.

items.name: MATLAB
items.description: Numerical computing environment and programming language used for matrix operations, data analysis, algorithm prototyping, and engineering simulations.

items.name: PL/SQL
items.description: Oracle's procedural extension of SQL, used to write stored procedures, functions, and triggers that implement business logic inside Oracle databases.

items.name: Python
items.description: High-level, general-purpose programming language known for its readable syntax, widely used for web development, data science, automation, and scripting.

items.name: R
items.description: Programming language and environment focused on statistical computing and graphics, commonly used for data analysis and academic research.

items.name: Scratch
items.description: Block-based visual programming language and online platform designed to teach programming concepts to children and beginners.

items.name: Solidity
items.description: Statically typed programming language designed for writing smart contracts that run on the Ethereum blockchain and compatible platforms.

items.name: SQL
items.description: Standard programming language used to query, update, and manage data stored in relational database systems.

items.name: Swift
items.description: Statically typed, compiled programming language developed by Apple for building applications on iOS, macOS, and other Apple platforms.

items.name: Transact-SQL
items.description: Microsoft's procedural extension of SQL used in SQL Server and Azure SQL Database for querying data and implementing stored procedures and triggers.

items.name: VB.NET
items.description: Object-oriented programming language on the .NET platform, evolved from classic Visual Basic, used mainly for building Windows desktop and enterprise applications.

items.name: VBA
items.description: Scripting language embedded in Microsoft Office applications, used to automate repetitive tasks and build custom functionality within documents and spreadsheets.

items.name: Visual Basic
items.description: Event-driven programming language and development environment originally created by Microsoft for building Windows applications with a simplified, beginner-friendly syntax.

items.name: ActionScript
items.description: Object-oriented scripting language originally used with Adobe Flash to create interactive animations and web applications, now largely obsolete.

items.name: AJAX
items.description: Technique for making web browsers exchange data with a server asynchronously in the background, allowing pages to update content without a full reload.

items.name: CSS
items.description: Stylesheet language used to control the visual presentation of HTML documents, including layout, colors, fonts, and responsive design.

items.name: HTML
items.description: Markup language used to structure content on web pages, defining elements like text, links, images, and forms.

items.name: HTML/CSS
items.description: Combined use of the markup language HTML for structuring web content and CSS for styling its visual presentation, forming the core of front-end web development.

items.name: HTML5
items.description: Version of HTML that adds semantic elements, multimedia support, and APIs for building modern interactive web applications without relying on plugins.

items.name: JavaScript
items.description: Scripting language used to add interactivity and dynamic behavior to web pages, and also used server-side and in many application environments.

items.name: Liquid
items.description: Template language used to embed dynamic content and logic into web pages, commonly used for building themes on the Shopify e-commerce platform.

items.name: Perl
items.description: General-purpose scripting language known for strong text-processing capabilities, historically popular for system administration and web CGI scripts.

items.name: PHP
items.description: Server-side scripting language designed for web development, used to generate dynamic web pages and interact with databases.

items.name: PowerShell
items.description: Command-line shell and scripting language used for task automation and configuration management, particularly on Windows and cloud systems.

items.name: Ruby
items.description: General-purpose, dynamic programming language known for its clean syntax and readability, widely used for web development via frameworks like Rails.

items.name: Sass
items.description: CSS preprocessor that adds features like variables, nesting, and mixins to make writing and maintaining stylesheets more efficient.

items.name: TypeScript
items.description: Statically typed superset of JavaScript that compiles to plain JavaScript, adding type checking to help catch errors during development.

items.name: VBScript
items.description: Lightweight scripting language developed by Microsoft, historically used for automating tasks in Windows and for client-side scripting in Internet Explorer.

items.name: XAML
items.description: Markup language used to define user interfaces declaratively in .NET applications, such as those built with WPF or UWP.

items.name: Bash
items.description: Unix shell and command language used for interacting with the operating system and writing automation scripts, common on Linux and macOS.

items.name: Batch Script
items.description: Scripting language used to automate sequences of commands on Windows systems via the command-line interpreter.

items.name: C
items.description: Low-level, general-purpose programming language known for its efficiency and close relationship to hardware, widely used in operating systems and embedded software.

items.name: C++
items.description: General-purpose programming language extending C with object-oriented and generic programming features, used in performance-critical applications like games and systems software.

items.name: C/C++
items.description: Pairing of the C and C++ programming languages, often grouped together due to their shared syntax and use in systems-level and performance-critical software.

items.name: KornShell (ksh)
items.description: Unix command-line shell and scripting language that combines features of the Bourne shell and C shell, used for interactive command execution and shell scripting.

items.name: Objective-C
items.description: General-purpose, object-oriented programming language that extends C with Smalltalk-style messaging, historically the primary language for macOS and iOS application development.
